title: Kafka Configuration
description: Learn the key broker, producer, and consumer configuration properties for production-ready Kafka deployments.

data.text: Kafka's behavior is controlled through thousands of configuration properties spread across brokers, producers, and consumers. Getting the right settings is essential for throughput, durability, and operational stability. This lesson covers the most impactful properties for production workloads.

Broker settings affect cluster behavior, replication, and disk usage. The most critical properties control how leaders are elected, how data is retained, and how many concurrent connections the broker will accept.

rows: Directories where Kafka stores partition logs. Use separate disks for better I/O throughput.
Default number of partitions for auto-created topics. Set explicitly per topic in production.
Default replication factor for auto-created topics. Use 3 in production for fault tolerance.
Minimum number of replicas that must acknowledge a write for the producer to consider it successful.
How long to retain log segments before deleting them.
Number of threads for background I/O operations. Increase for high-throughput clusters.

data.text: Producer settings control batching, compression, and delivery guarantees. The `acks` property is the most important for durability: it determines how many replicas must confirm a write before the producer receives an acknowledgment.

data.title: High-Throughput Producer Configuration (C#)
data.content: Optimized Confluent.Kafka producer settings for throughput and reliability.

data.title: Enable Idempotence
data.text: Always set `enable.idempotence=true` in production. It adds sequence numbers to messages, preventing duplicates even when retries occur.

Consumer settings control how often offsets are committed, how partitions are assigned, and how the consumer recovers from failures. The `max.poll.records` property limits the number of records returned in a single poll call, preventing long-running processing from blocking rebalances.

data.content: Confluent.Kafka consumer settings for production resilience.

data.definition:
flowchart TD
    subgraph Producer Config
        P1[acks] --> P1V{acks=all?}
        P1V -->|yes| P1H[High durability]
        P1V -->|no| P1L[Lower latency]
        P2[linger.ms] --> P2H[Higher throughput]
        P3[compression.type] --> P3S[Smaller messages]
    end

    subgraph Consumer Config
        C1[enable.auto.commit] --> C1M[Manual commit]
        C2[max.poll.records] --> C2L[Limit batch size]
        C3[session.timeout.ms] --> C3D[Failure detection]
    end

    P1H --> K[(Kafka Cluster)]
    P1L --> K
    P2H --> K
    P3S --> K
    C1M --> K
    C2L --> K
    C3D --> K
data.caption: Key producer and consumer configuration paths

data.title: Configuration Checklist
points: Enable producer idempotence to prevent duplicates on retry.
Use manual offset commits in consumers for at-least-once processing.
data.takeaway: Configuration is the difference between a Kafka cluster that survives a broker failure and one that does not.
